title: Fuzzing-Inspired Adversarial Prompt Generation for Safety Evals

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain from coverage-guided fuzzing to novel safety tests to addressing benchmark contamination. Static benchmarks becoming stale is a well-documented problem this directly addresses.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt mutation is feasible with standard tools, but building a coverage-guided fuzzer with behavioral diversity signals requires solid ML fundamentals and careful engineering.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Could scope to a single model and single mutation strategy, but the full pipeline (mutations, coverage signal, comparison with fixed benchmarks) requires sustained effort beyond a quick experiment.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple mature frameworks already exist: LLM-Fuzzer (USENIX Security 2024) scales jailbreak assessment using fuzzing, PROMPTFUZZ (2024) directly applies fuzzing techniques to prompt generation, Palo Alto Unit42 published coverage-guided prompt fuzzing results across open/closed models, and an in-browser LLM-guided fuzzing framework for prompt injection testing was published in 2025. The core idea of applying coverage-guided fuzzing to adversarial prompt generation for safety evaluation is well-explored with published tools and benchmarks.
